title: A.R.M.O.R. health report of one node
description: How one node of any family (radar, solar, electrical, alarm, hmi) is doing, in the same words for all of them: how long it has been up and why it last restarted, how much memory it has, the link it reaches the network by, how often it lost the broker and the last thing it complained of. Published to armor/health/{node_id} every minute or so (never retained). It is not the presence message of a radar (health.schema.json, armor/node/{node_id}/health): that one says only whether the node is there. A report is information: it carries no command and nothing is decided by it on the node.

family.description: What kind of node says it.

firmware.description: The firmware version, three parts or four from 0.8.0.

board.description: The board profile the firmware was built for (s3-wifi, s3-eth, lcd7box ...).

uptime_s.description: Seconds since the node started. A value smaller than the one before is a restart.

reset_reason.description: Why the node started this time: power_on, external (the reset pin), software (a restart it asked for, an update included), panic, int_wdt, task_wdt, other_wdt, deep_sleep, brownout, sdio, usb, jtag, efuse, power_glitch, cpu_lockup or unknown.

heap_min.description: The least heap that has been free since the node started, in bytes (never more than heap_free).

heap_internal_free.description: Bytes of the internal memory free now. heap_free counts the external RAM (PSRAM) too, so on a board that has it that figure never looks short; this one is the memory the radio, the drivers and the task stacks need. Absent from a node that does not read it.

heap_internal_min.description: The least internal memory that has been free since the node started, in bytes (never more than heap_internal_free). Sent with heap_internal_free.

heap_internal_largest.description: The biggest single block of internal memory that could be allocated now, in bytes (never more than heap_internal_free): a heap in pieces fails a big request while the total looks fine. Sent with heap_internal_free.

psram_free.description: Bytes of the external RAM free now; absent from a board that has none (or whose external RAM did not start).

link.description: How the node reaches the network: the Wi-Fi station, the Ethernet port, or neither.

link_up.description: Whether that link is up (associated, or a cable with a carrier) and has an address; false whenever link is none.

rssi_dbm.description: Wi-Fi signal strength in dBm; only on a Wi-Fi link that is up.

broker_reconnects.description: How many times the node has connected to the broker since it started (the first connection counts one, so a node that never lost it says 1).

low_stack_tasks.description: How many tasks of the node have less than 512 bytes of stack left at their worst.

last_error.description: The last error the node logged, cut to fit; absent when it has logged none since it started.

control_state.description: Optional: whether the node does its work (running), has paused it for a while or has it off until it is resumed (standby). Absent on a firmware that cannot be controlled.

control_since_ms.description: Optional, when paused or standby: the wall-clock time (ms) it began; 0 if the clock is not set.

control_by.description: Optional, when paused or standby: the person the order was for.

control_until_s.description: Optional, when paused: seconds left until it resumes by itself.

maintenance.description: Optional: the maintenance flag is on (the server holds back the node-offline alert).

maintenance_until_s.description: Optional, when maintenance is on: seconds left.
